title: Faces of the sangha
hookLine: wise, powerful, forgetful, proud, gentle: all were welcome

cards: Line them up the way the texts remember them. A man the texts call foremost in wisdom. His friend, foremost in powers.
A slow monk who couldn't keep a single verse in his head. A former charioteer too proud to take advice from anyone. A cousin so gentle he served as attendant, bringing water and keeping the door.
Different speeds, different tempers, different flaws, all in one robe color. None of them was turned away for being who he was.

teach.b: First, the word. Sangha means community, an assembly. In the narrow sense it's the order of monks and nuns; in a wider sense, some Buddhists use it for everyone who walks the path together.
It's the third of the Three Jewels, beside the Buddha and the dhamma, the things a Buddhist goes to for refuge.

teach.h: WISE AND POWERFUL, SIDE BY SIDE.
teach.b: Second, the wise and the powerful. Sariputta and Moggallana, the two chief disciples, are the faces people expect: the texts praise one for wisdom and the other for power.
Third, the slow and the proud. In a commentary story, Culapanthaka's own brother told him to leave the order, because he couldn't learn one verse.
The Buddha handed him a clean white cloth instead, and as he rubbed it gray, he understood.
And Channa, the former charioteer, was so stubborn that the Buddha, before he died, said the monks should give him the higher penalty: no one would speak to him or advise him.
The Vinaya says that silence brought him to his senses, and he too awakened.
Fourth, one path, different paces. Ananda, gentle and loyal, was still not awakened when the Buddha died. The sangha was never a gallery of finished people.
It was a room where people at very different points sat side by side.
And the welcome had a shape. It wasn't approval of every flaw. Channa's pride was met with a hard silence, but the silence was meant to bring him back, not to push him out.

how: Buddhists go for refuge to the Buddha, the dhamma and the sangha, often reciting the three refuges in Pali at the start of a gathering, and teachers retell the disciples' stories to show that people of every temperament walked the path.

o: the community walking the Buddhist path
the teaching the Buddha passed down
a meditation hall where monks gather

games.q: faces of the sangha: tap the pairs.
p: not yet awake when the Buddha died

s: only the wisest disciples were allowed to stay
a slow monk, a proud charioteer and a gentle attendant all stayed, each at his own pace.
Channa's pride was met with silence from the community
before he died the Buddha said the monks should give Channa the higher penalty: no one would speak to him or advise him.
the sangha is the third of the Three Jewels
Buddha, dhamma and sangha: the three refuges.

games.q: the Buddha has died, and Ananda, his gentle attendant, is still not awakened. where does that leave him?
o: outside the sangha until he awakens.
still in the sangha, at his own pace.
leading the sangha in the Buddha's place.
games.why: the sangha was never a gallery of finished people. Ananda sat beside the awakened, walking the same path at a different pace.

practice: Bring one friend to mind, and let one of their flaws come up, the habit that wears on you: running late, talking over people, forgetting what you told them.
Don't fix it, and don't excuse it; just set it beside everything else they are, the way the sangha set the slow monk beside the wise one. The flaw is real, and the friend is more than the flaw.

wordCard.voice: Sangha. The community: wise, powerful, forgetful, proud and gentle, all welcomed and practicing side by side. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali saṅgha: community, assembly. The third of the Three Jewels.

carryVoice: Your line: all were welcome. Wise or slow, proud or gentle, there was room. That's day seven hundred seventy-nine.
